thread.title: Gorilla Glass Maker Corning Stock Breaks Out After iPhone XS Launch

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Gorilla Glass Maker Corning Stock Breaks Out After iPhone XS Launch
text:
Specialty glass products maker Corning ( GLW ) saw its stock shatter through a resistance level on Thursday. The bullish move came after key customer Apple ( AAPL ) showed off three new big-screen iPhones at an event Wednesday.
X Corning stock jumped 3.1% to 35.06 on the stock market today . It broke out of a cup-with-handle base at a buy point of 34.25. It had been building the base for 33 weeks after retreating from a 17-year high of 35.10 on Jan. 19. It touched that recent high in intraday trading on Thursday.
The Corning, N.Y.-based company makes products for a host of electronics, communications and industrial customers. It has five business segments: Optical Communications, Display Technologies, Specialty Materials, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences.
Its Optical Communications segment makes optical fiber products and accounted for 35% of Corning's sales in 2017. Its Display Technologies unit makes glass substrates for television and PC displays and represented 30% of sales last year.
Makes Gorilla Glass Covers For iPhones Specialty Materials is the unit that makes Gorilla Glass display covers for smartphones like the iPhone and other mobile devices. The unit also makes products for customers in semiconductors, aerospace and defense, and other industries. The unit represented 14% of Corning's sales in 2017.
Environmental Technologies makes ceramic substrates and filter products for emissions control in gasoline- and diesel-powered vehicles. It accounted for 11% of Corning's sales last year. Finally, the company's Life Sciences unit supplies laboratory products for researchers and drugmakers; it contributed about 9% of revenue in 2017.
Corning Chief Financial Officer Tony Tripeny spoke at the Deutsche Bank Technology Conference on Thursday. He discussed the company's strategic investments and cash return program for shareholders, according to Seeking Alpha .
He noted that the company is seeing "strength across all of our businesses." Corning also is seeing new business opportunities such as supplying Gorilla Glass for automobiles, Tripeny said.
